## Use 'AudioConversionMEL' instead.

```{r}
library(tuneR)
library(seewave)
```

Reading in file

```{r}
audio_data <- readWave("671658014.180928183606-AW.wav", from = 0, to = .1, units = "hours")

```

Extracting Raw Audio Samples

```{r}
raw_samples <- audio_data@left
```

Creating a Time-Domain Tabular Dataset

```{r}
sampling_rate <- audio_data@samp.rate
#16 bit

#length(sampling_rate)

time_points <- seq(from = 0, by = 1/sampling_rate, length.out = length(raw_samples))
time_domain_df <- data.frame(Time = time_points, Amplitude = raw_samples)
```

Creating a Frequency-Domain Tabular Dataset (e.g., using Spectrogram)

```{r}
spectrogram_data <- spectro(audio_data@left, 
                            f = sampling_rate,
                            wn = "hanning",
                            collevels = seq(-80, 0 ,1),
                            plot = TRUE)
#represents the actual pressure oscillations of a sound wave, not its amplitude

```

The spectrogram_data object contains time, frequency, and amplitude information, which can then be restructured into a data frame.

```{r}
library(reshape2)
library(dplyr)
```

```{r}
#AI Generated
#Error in code


# Extract and melt time and frequency data
time_melted <- melt(spectrogram_data$time, value.name = "Time") %>%
  mutate(TimeIndex = row_number())
frequency_melted <- melt(spectrogram_data$freq, value.name = "Frequency") %>%
  mutate(FrequencyIndex = row_number())

# Combine amplitude data with time and frequency
amplitude_df <- as.data.frame(spectrogram_data$amp)
colnames(amplitude_df) <- paste0("Freq_", 1:ncol(amplitude_df)) # Rename columns if needed

amplitude_df$TimeIndex <- row_number()

# Join to create the final frequency-domain data frame
frequency_domain_df <- amplitude_df %>%
  left_join(time_melted, by = "TimeIndex") %>%
  left_join(frequency_melted, by = "FrequencyIndex") %>%
  select(Time, Frequency, Amplitude = Freq_1) # Adjust 'Freq_1' based on your spectrogram output
```

```{r}
# Compute MFCCs with default settings
mfcc_coeffs <- melfcc(audio_wave)


mfcc_coeffs2 <- melfcc(audio_wave, wintime = 0.1, hoptime = .1, numcep = 13, bwidth = 20)


# The result is a matrix where each row is a time frame and each column is a coefficient.
# View the dimensions of the resulting matrix
dim(mfcc_coeffs)

dim(mfcc_coeffs2)


# Inspect the first few rows of the MFCC matrix
head(mfcc_coeffs)

```
